text: Employers need to be proactive in creating workplaces that are inclusive, flexible and capable of supporting workers at all life stages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And for the Government, this shift requires a fundamental change in how we support the workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today's seniors are better educated and more skilled than the generations before them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Future seniors will be even more so, reflecting the high cohort participation in our universities in our population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Seniors therefore offer a growing wealth of human capital and many of them want to contribute meaningfully to our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Supporting seniors today is no longer just about extending working years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It requires planning ahead to enable sustainable careers across later stages of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are strengthening support across mid-career and later-career transitions through the Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: More than 10 years ago, tripartite partners started removing barriers for seniors who wanted to keep working.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A major step was to progressively raise the retirement and re-employment ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These moves have helped more seniors stay employed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These changes matter because they do more than set legal limits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They shape social norms around ageing and work, giving seniors confidence to stay on and giving employers the clarity to plan for and retain experienced workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I want to assure Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari that these changes have made a difference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Internationally, this puts Singapore among the leaders – for workers in their 60s, we rank fifth compared to OECD countries for labour force participation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But for workers in their 50s, we rank only 23rd.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We agree with Ms Jessica Tan's call on the need to strengthen career support for mature and senior PMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We need to do more work upstream, to support workers who may be leaving the workforce earlier than they need to or earlier than they would like to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is why MOM, together with NTUC and the SNEF, convened the Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment in July last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment reflects a shared responsibility, by workers, employers and the Government, to respond to longer, more varied careers for our seniors, including PMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With longer careers ahead, support cannot wait until workers are near retirement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: From our engagements, both employers and seniors told us that earlier training and career guidance are essential to keep skills fresh, open new pathways and ensure every stage of a longer working life remains meaningful and productive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment is therefore studying recommendations across the senior's career journey, including during mid-career transitions and later-career stages, where timely interventions can make the greatest difference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Just as good physical health supports longer and better physical lives, good career health supports longer working lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And like physical health, career health benefits from early, regular check-ins and career planning, not only when problems arise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is especially important for many who are mid-career in their 40s and 50s, adapting to new roles, technologies or sectors, while balancing work and family commitments and responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These pivotal years determine how long and how well they can continue working.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Yet working adults often face this journey alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Unlike the structured education and career guidance that one might find in schools, working adults receive less structured support to help them make sense of options at this stage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is why, as the Minister highlighted earlier, we are strengthening and broadening Career Health SG by working with and developing the Career and Employment Services sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will grow the sector so that there is a variety of good quality services to cater to different segments of seniors, to help them plan ahead, navigate transitions and build sustainable careers over a longer working life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With the right guidance, later-stage career transitions can open new doors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Participants, like 61-year-old Mr Eddie Sng and 55-year-old Ms Mabel Lee, show how this works in practice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After attending WSG-supported career guidance workshops, both began to see career transitions as growth opportunities rather than professional endings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, Eddie, a former logistics managing director, is now pursuing logistics advisory work while creating digital content.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mabel, a former photographer and marketing professional, has secured a part-time marketing manager role while building her photography teaching practice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Their journeys show how strategic career guidance enables older workers to rethink their options, make confident transitions and continue contributing meaningfully.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Building on these early successes, WSG will work with partners to scale up the provision of career guidance for later-stage careers and integrate these programmes into its regular career guidance offerings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But career guidance by a third-party is not enough.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many seniors who are already in employment need clarity on how long they can stay in a role, whether their job will evolve and how they might work differently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are insights that only their employers can provide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Employers must therefore have deliberate conversations with their workers to plan for job redesign, identify skills needed to seize future job opportunities and adjust work arrangements over time as part of regular workforce planning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This Structured Career Planning (SCP) should not just be a structured conversation, but should be also structured as part of routine HR processes within the company.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Under the Part-Time Re-employment Grant, employers are required to send management and HR representatives to SCP workshops, to gain knowledge and skillsets to conduct SCP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: What we have learnt is that SCP works best when it starts earlier, not only when one has reached the age for re-employment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Strengthening career planning earlier helps seniors stay confident and employable, while giving employers clearer sight of how to develop and deploy their workforce over longer careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari rightly asked how we can intervene at the mid-career stage to boost continued employability before workers reach their late 50s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, building on the positive experience with SCP, we will therefore give a stronger push for employers to adopt regular SCP conversations earlier in their employees' careers and explore how SCP can be more systematically embedded into HR training and certification requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will enable employers and workers to proactively redesign jobs, adjust work arrangements and build resilience over longer careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As workers move into later stages of their careers, some may wish to continue full-time work, others prefer reduced hours or more focused roles, while some require adjustments over time as their priorities, their health status or physical abilities change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Whether seniors can continue contributing depends largely on how workplaces adapt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari and Mr Shawn Loh have asked for longer extensions to the Senior Employment Credit, and whether the scheme will be studied beyond 2027.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond these measures, we also need to rethink traditional job designs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: What does age-friendly work look like in practice?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There is no one-size-fits-all model that will work for every company and it will likely be different across industries and job roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through the Alliance for Action on Empowering Multi-Stage Careers for Mature Workers (AfA-EMW), we are working with organisations including intermediaries to test practical models, which can give employers greater confidence to act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, under the AfA-EMW, the pilot by QED Changemakers gives us a glimpse of how we can unlock senior expertise in new ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: By connecting experienced senior professionals with companies that need their expertise on a project basis, senior professionals can continue contributing meaningfully, sharing decades of experience, staying active and earning an income, while companies, especially SMEs, get access to seasoned leadership when they need it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Another example explores how simple job redesign can keep experienced bus captains on the road, safely and sustainably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Tower Transit is piloting new work arrangements that allow senior bus captains to continue working safely and confidently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With more balanced shifts, job rotation and lighter duties, seniors can keep contributing, while the company retains experience, maintains service reliability, and supports the next generation of bus captains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These prototypes are being developed and will feed into the Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment's recommendations, translating good ideas into scalable practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As seniors remain economically active for longer, work must also remain safe and sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Minister of State Dinesh Vasu Dash will share more detail about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These efforts reflect a holistic approach to senior employment, to help seniors continue to contribute meaningfully, in ways that work for them, for their employers and for our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Across both mid- and later-career stages, navigating transitions remains a key challenge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Workers need clearer pathways to plan their next steps, while employers need guidance on age-friendly workforce design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For individuals, this would help them better navigate and access the relevant career, skills and employment support in accordance with their needs, including allowing them to plan earlier for their later-stage career transitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For employers, they would be able to access practical resources and the network of partners to support them in designing age-friendly workplaces and strengthen multi-generational teams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For partners, this would be a platform for them to test and scale new initiatives, new innovative practices, including those emerging from AfA-EMW.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This centre could be co-located with existing career centres, so individuals who need job search assistance can receive more holistic support across the various aspects of career planning, skills and employment, rather than navigating these services separately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In this way, we shift the focus from managing exits to enabling longer, meaningful participation at work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked when the Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment will share its recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment was established last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After communicating and exchanging views with various parties, the Workgroup concluded that as Singaporeans' careers extend, we must assist employees with career planning earlier, support employers in redesigning job roles and ensure that relevant systems and incentive measures are practical and feasible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For employees, this means receiving support for career guidance and skills training earlier, enabling smooth transitions while they still have options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For employers, this means receiving clearer support to retain experienced employees, redesign job roles and provide flexible work arrangements that are more suitable for older workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For the Government, this means strengthening the overall career and employment ecosystem, ensuring the viability and sustainability of longer careers through career guidance, skills training and employment incentives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But this is not a challenge unique to seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Across the workforce, workers are navigating more frequent changes as our economy restructures and technology reshapes jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This calls for stronger systems that help all workers and employers manage transitions more deliberately and responsibly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Employers and especially their HR teams are critical enablers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: HR sits at the intersection of skills and career development, job redesign and employment practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are establishing clearer benchmarks of what "good" looks like.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Singapore Opportunity Index gives employers and workers a data-driven yardstick to see how the best workplaces shape outcomes like pay, progression and retention, enabling employers to make sharper talent decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond recognising top performers, we are progressively releasing detailed reports and advisory support to help all 1,500 organisations covered by the Singapore Opportunity Index improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To turn these insights into real gains for workers and businesses, the workgroup will also make recommendations to uplift the HR profession in key areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SNEF is leading a multi‑agency effort to pilot a National HR Leadership Programme, together with NTUC and our local HR institutes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The programme aims to strengthen Singapore's local HR leaders through international exposure, experiential learning, mentoring and networking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, we are preparing HR for AI-driven change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As AI accelerates transformation across sectors, stronger and more systematic HR capability becomes even more critical.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AI can automate repetitive tasks like scheduling interviews and handling routine queries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It can also surface workforce trends more quickly, helping HR to spot skill gaps earlier and design better development and deployment strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But let us be clear here: AI is not here to replace the human in HR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AI can take care of the processes, but only humans can take care of people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This shift towards human-AI collaboration presents opportunities for HR to be more strategic, more developmental and more human-centered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked how we are equipping HR to be more AI-driven.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: MOM is working with the Ministry of Digital Development and Information and the Infocomm Media Development Authority under the National AI Impact Programme to develop AI fluency amongst HR professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In parallel, NTUC is developing a framework to help companies with limited AI experience, especially smaller SMEs navigate the complexity of AI adoption for HR by consolidating existing resources for AI readiness assessment, training, applicable grants and widely adopted AI tools for HR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Looking ahead, MOM, WSG and IHRP will refresh the HR Jobs Transformation Map this year to provide clear guidance on two fronts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: One, how AI will transform HR jobs and two, how its impact on the wider workforce will change the demands on HR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The the Tripartite Workgroup on Human Capital Capability Development will also consider Ms Tan's suggestions as part of its broader review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Third, we must expand professional HR practice to more organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As our workforce becomes more diverse and employment issues more complex, organisations need HR that meet high standards, possess future-ready competencies and are committed to continuous professional development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This need was recognised back in 2020 when the NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce recommended mandating HR certification for larger firms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, such a significant change could not happen overnight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is why we have spent the last five years laying the groundwork to strengthen the value of HR certification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A recent study by MOM economists showed that the IHRP certification delivered measurable improvements in both wage outcomes and employment prospects of certified professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This ultimately translates into benefits for both firms and workers, as evidenced by the greater range of career development initiatives – such as workforce planning and career guidance – implemented in organisations with certified HR professionals compared to those without.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With this critical mass established, we are now ready to take the next step.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We need a broader coverage of certified HR professionals who can embed best practices like structured career planning, which I mentioned earlier, to strengthen employee engagement and in turn business productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We just cannot afford to leave this to chance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked if the Government will consider mandating IHRP certification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For firms who may not have dedicated HR, MOM is working with partners to uplift the wider career and employment services ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As mentioned by Minister, through the Alliance for Action on Advancing Career and Employment Services (AfA ACES), we are working with private career and employment service providers to pilot new initiatives and services to support workers of diverse profiles in their career journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These efforts – from uplifting HR capabilities to partnering ecosystem players – are part of a longer-term vision under the Economic Strategy Review's Committee on Human Capital, which I co-chair, to build a future-ready jobs and skills ecosystem where employers invest in people, HR is a strategic partner and workers can move more confidently across roles and sectors over a longer working life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As the economy evolves, more workers may face job displacement, not because they lack ability, but because of business restructuring or failure or economic cycles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Even with stronger HR capabilities and better career support systems, job transitions may still be difficult, especially when the change happens abruptly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To help workers through such transitions, we introduced the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme in April last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This scheme provides temporary financial relief to involuntarily unemployed individuals, helping them transition into suitable new roles rather than rushing into poor job matches.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Ng Chee Meng and Mr Patrick Tay asked whether we would consider increasing the current qualifying income cap.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As the scheme has only been rolled out last year, we will conduct a review when we have more experience, including on key parameters such as the qualifying income, to ensure the scheme remains well-targeted and sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Building on this, the ESR's Committee on Managing the Impact of Restructuring is studying how we can support workers more proactively and how we can extend meaningful support to more groups, including PMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For instance, as Minister said, this could include requiring earlier notice of retrenchment from employers, leveraging networks of trade associations and chambers to provide more targeted job matching in sectors with more PME job openings and expanding the scope of support under Career Conversion Programmes to help more workers with the transition into growth jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These efforts reflect a shift from reacting to job loss, to actively supporting career transitions, guided by strong tripartite partnerships and closer alignment between skills, jobs and industry needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond transition support, our employment laws are important to ensure our workers are adequately protected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many Singaporeans may not realise that the Employment Act profoundly shapes our everyday working lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It sets out the basic terms and conditions of employment, such as timely salary payments, overtime pay and sick leave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As the Employment Act covers almost all employees in Singapore, we must always strike a careful balance between protecting employees and giving space for employers to thrive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our workforce profile is different, work arrangements are more varied and businesses are operating in a more competitive environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: That is why the tripartite partners convened the Tripartite Workgroup on the Employment Act Review in August last year, to review key parts of the Act in a balanced way, protecting workers who need it most while supporting business flexibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Pritam Singh and Mr Patrick Tay have asked for an update on the main areas of review for the Employment Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Pritam Singh also asked if the review can include a public consultation in parallel with tripartite negotiations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: What we heard from workers and employers was clear: different groups need different forms of protection and flexibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For lower-wage employees, time-based protections still matter and overtime pay remains an important part of their income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As wages rise and the workforce profile evolves, we will review Part 4 of the Employment Act to ensure these protections remain well-targeted at workers who need them most.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For employers, greater flexibility is needed to manage costs, redesign jobs and stay competitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Done right, this can also benefit workers, by allowing employers and employees to negotiate mutually beneficial arrangements that meet individual needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Employees who believe that they are affected by unreasonable or unjustified clauses can seek assistance from their unions, TAFEP or MOM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will study how to streamline and clarify key provisions, so that they are easier to understand and comply with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through this Tripartite Workgroup, we are strengthening protections where they matter most, while keeping our labour framework practical and responsive as careers lengthen and workplaces evolve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Taken together, these efforts reflect a simple principle: as work changes, our protections must evolve alongside it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Whether it is supporting workers through restructuring or updating the Employment Act, our aim is the same – to ensure workers and employers can adapt with confidence to the future of work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Career longevity is not simply about staying employed for longer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is about enabling Singaporeans to remain productive, adaptable and engaged across different stages of their lives and enabling employers to continue drawing on the full range of experience, skills and capabilities in a tight labour force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This effort cannot be carried by any single party alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Minister Tan See Leng has set out MOM’s bold agenda to equip our businesses to seize emerging opportunities and chart a course for growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As we build the economy of tomorrow, our commitment is that each and every worker will be supported and that no worker will be left behind.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This is the spirit of a “we first” Singapore, where everyone has their place and can participate with dignity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Most importantly, all contributions, particularly those from our vulnerable workers, will have to be recognised and uplifted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In my speech today, I will elaborate on three areas: first, our tripartite efforts to uplift lower-wage workers and how we will progress this work in the next-bound; second, our drive to strengthen workplace safety and health, such that our workers continue to return home safely to their loved ones; and third, how we will continue to support our migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: These efforts embody the very heart of our social compact – our promise to walk with our lower-wage workers every step of the way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As you contribute to Singapore’s progress, so too will you share in the rewards and opportunities that accompany that progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We have forged over time a distinctly Singaporean approach to supporting our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We have uplifted wages for lower-wage workers without putting their jobs at risk through the PWM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: PWMs serve as wage ladders across nine sectors and occupations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: These are negotiated by tripartite partners with reference to considerations such as productivity and business conditions, ensuring that wage growth does not exceed what the sector or occupation can bear.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: PWMs also map out clear pathways for training and progression.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Wage increments are therefore sustainable for employers, as they come alongside productivity growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Lower-wage workers not covered by PWMs may benefit from the LQS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Firms must pay their local workers at least the LQS if they hire foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Lower-wage workers receive additional support through the Workfare Income Supplement scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This scheme supplements their incomes and helps them save for retirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The 20th income percentile for a full time resident employee is about $2,800 currently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: So, the Workfare Income Supplement qualifying monthly wage cap of $3,000 continues to target Singaporean workers with earnings in the bottom 20%, with some support to those who are slightly above.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We have and will continue to review the Workfare Income Supplement regularly to ensure it remains effective in supporting our lower-wage workers, complementing the PWM and LQS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Mr Melvin Yong highlighted business transformation is crucial as it enables sustainable wage growth through productivity improvement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: It also unlocks opportunities for lower-wage workers to take up higher value-added job roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Recognising that this is a process that takes time and to cushion the impact on business costs, the Government introduced the PWCS at Budget 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Third, we enable progression of our lower-wage workers through support for training and upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Schemes such as the Workfare Skills Support (WSS) reduce the opportunity cost of training for lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This opens doors for workers to move up in their careers, including progressing up PWM job ladders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Our approach had delivered tangible outcomes for lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The LQS requirement was also broadened in 2022, such that firms hiring foreign manpower are required to pay LQS to all their local workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This ensures that no Singaporean worker is left behind.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Another 104,000 lower-wage workers not covered by PWMs are therefore supported by the LQS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This has made a significant difference for the incomes of lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Workers in PWM sectors have and will continue to see significant improvement in their wages as our economy grows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As an illustration, the baseline wage requirement for entry-level office and commercial cleaners has increased by about 50% cumulatively since 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: By 2028, it will be $2,420, which is almost twice the requirement in 2021, which was then $1,274.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Likewise, compared to 2021, entry-level outsourced security officers can also expect to earn a higher monthly gross wage by about 40% more in 2026, and 60% in 2028.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This is progress that we can be proud of – progress that reflects the collective resolve of unions, employers and the Government working in unison to improve the livelihoods of our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: But we are committed to going even further.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We will build on our efforts across each of these areas, to further uplift and upskill our lower-wage workers and broaden the range of good jobs as recommended by the Economic Strategy Review Committee.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: First and foremost, we must sustain our momentum in uplifting wages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In 2025, tripartite partners announced updated wage schedules for Retail, In-house Security, Administrators and Drivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The remaining PWM sectors will negotiate their next-bound of wage schedules increases later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Raising the LQS to keep pace with wage growth ensures that locals are employed meaningfully, rather than in token jobs just so that firms can hire foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Second, we will spur business transformation to raise productivity and create better jobs, including for our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Mr Melvin Yong would be pleased to note that MOM will be introducing various initiatives in support of this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: For example, the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant (Job Redesign+) will be rolled out in March this year to provide enhanced funding support for job redesign and workforce transformation as part of the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package .

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We will also launch the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit this year, to provide additional support for workforce development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Businesses have also shared their concerns around near-term economic uncertainties and manpower costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Businesses will not be left alone to deal with cost pressures as they seek to do their part for our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This builds on four earlier enhancements to PWCS, most recently in 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Since the scheme was introduced in 2022, PWCS has supported wage improvement for lower-wage workers, even as firms undertake the longer journey of transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: For wage increases given between 2022 and 2024, the Government provided about $3.6 billion of PWCS funding to over 110,000 employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: These wage increases have been meaningful – the median monthly increase supported by PWCS was about $250, across more than 710,000 workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about the outcomes of the PWCS, including how it had been tied to business transformation, sector productivity and worker upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Uplifting wage outcomes for lower-wage workers and narrowing the wage gap with the median is, in itself, a key objective of this Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I have shared earlier of how we have performed well on these measures and these are measures in real income terms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: But ultimately, productivity needs to rise for wages to be sustained.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Raising productivity is, therefore, a key focus of the PWM as it links wage growth to skills development, career progression and job redesign.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This is complemented by our enterprise grants that enable business transformation and job redesign, and support for upskilling, such as the Workfare Skills Support scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: PWCS provides transitional co-funding for wage increases given to lower-wage workers, allowing businesses the space to restructure business processes and reap productivity improvements There are many good examples of forward-looking companies which have moved to innovate and evolve in this area.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: ISS has benefited from the PWCS support in providing its lower-wage workers wage increases, as well as productivity improvements, through the various technology-enabled solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: For example, ISS' cleaning services now deploy a fleet of more than 130 cleaning autonomous robots, which have led to considerable gains in productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: ISS' investments in technology and automation have also unlocked opportunities for its workers to progress to more value-added roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: For example, Mr Arthur Lim, a healthcare cleaner under the PWM, has been able to take on more complex duties with greater technical requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Mr Lim tapped on upskilling opportunities, including those supported by the WSS scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: He is now proficient in operating specialised equipment, such as the ultraviolet disinfection machines and also manages enhanced healthcare cleaning protocols and contributes to infection control workflows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Mr Lim shares that learning these new skills has given him a renewed sense of purpose and contribution to his workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Likewise, there are F&B firms that are adapting to enhance their capabilities and boost their business performance, as stated in the Singapore Productivity Centre's recent Food Services Productivity Report.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: For example, Sushi Express leverages sushi robots and these have reduced the time taken to mould a piece of sushi to below 15 seconds, while improving production consistency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: With this PWCS' extension, we will continue to support businesses in doing so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In deciding on the enhancements, we took into account the current uncertainty in the economic and geopolitical landscape, business conditions as well as consultations with our tripartite partners among other factors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: And this actually higher than the 20% which was originally announced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The extended PWCS support in 2027 and 2028 will also have a higher minimum qualifying threshold for wage increases of $200, from $100.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This better encourages and rewards businesses that invest in transformation and workforce development in line with PWCS' objectives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We urge employers to take advantage of the Government's various forms of support, including the initiatives to be rolled out as part of the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package, such as the SkillsFuture WDG(JR+) and the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Employers can leverage these to further their respective transformation journeys and support their lower-wage workers in skills upgrading to perform higher value jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This brings me to our third area of focus – our support for lower-wage workers in upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As Ms Yeo Wan Ling observed, this will allow our workers to move alongside instead of being displaced by business transformation, so they can take on new roles and advance in their careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Minister Tan has outlined how Career Health SG empowers individuals to take charge of their careers and how we are evolving our SkillsFuture movement to refresh our jobs and skills ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: These are moves that will support all workers in their career planning and upskilling journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: However, lower-wage workers may face unique constraints in stepping away from their work to pursue training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This therefore becomes a catch 22 situation as taking time off to upskill may mean forgoing income that they may need for immediate expenses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Lower-wage workers can be assured that the Government understands these challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As announced at Budget 2025, trainees undertaking long-form courses will be supported with a training allowance significantly higher than the existing WSS support for short-form courses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: WSS (Level-Up) will support lower-wage workers in pursuing these more substantive forms of upskilling and reskilling, without needing to worry about making ends meet.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: To give just a few examples, retail workers can benefit from higher training allowances to undertake a Nitec qualification in Retail Services or a Diploma in Retail (Operations).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: At the same time, we will also enhance the WSS (Basic) scheme to support workers undertaking shorter training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: With the increase in the hourly training allowance, workers can now actively consider training without having a significant reduction in pay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We will also streamline the scheme to reduce complexity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Full qualifications are sets of related courses that result in a formal qualification, such as the WSQ Qualifications or Academic Continuing Education and Training Qualifications.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: These have been found to lead to better outcomes for trainees, compared to modules that do not lead to any formal qualifications.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Mr Melvin Yong suggested developing better AI-relevant skills pathways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: He would be glad to know that the courses supported by WSS include industry-relevant AI skills courses that are suitable for lower-wage workers, so that they will not be left behind amidst this AI transformation that we are currently undergoing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Employers must press on with wage increases for lower-wage workers and go the extra mile in redesigning jobs and business processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Workers should embrace opportunities for upskilling and chart new paths to build their careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: And Government will partner employers and workers through co-sharing the near-term costs of transformation and ensuring that training and skills upgrading remain accessible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Consumers can make their choices count by supporting businesses which pay Progressive Wages to lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: They can look out for and support businesses that may have attained the Progressive Wage Mark.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We are united with you, and we are here to support you in every way that we can.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: You can count on us for our support, and we will be here for the years to come as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Through the collective efforts and commitment of all stakeholders, our WSH performance has continued to improve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I am heartened by the steady progress towards our WSH 2028 goal of sustaining the fatal injury rate at below 1.0.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Singapore's workplace fatal injury rate for 2025 was 0.96% per 100,000 workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This is the lowest on record other than when COVID-19 disrupted work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: That said, we must not rest on our laurels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Every workplace death is a tragedy, and we must continue to stay vigilant in uplifting our WSH standards and to build a strong and sustainable WSH culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: There are many companies who have heeded this call, and I will cite one example.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Teambuild (ICPH) Pte Ltd, an SME in the manufacturing sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Teambuild has invested in technology to redesign work processes and create safer workplaces for their workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: By introducing the rebar mesh welding methods and machines, they have automated stackers for completed prefabricated, pre-finished volumetric construction units.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Teambuild has reduced the need for manual handling of these very heavy materials.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This has, in turn, brought down the musculoskeletal injuries amongst their workers and increased productivity at the same point, where they were able to improve productivity costs of about $180,000 per year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Teambuild's efforts show that when companies prioritise their workers' safety and health, they also build a more productive and sustainable business over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As the nature of work evolves and our workforce changes, new opportunities emerge alongside new challenges for workplace safety and health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The greater use of digital technology and an ageing workforce are two such examples.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Mr Melvin Yong emphasised the need to go beyond traditional high-risk industries and to pay greater attention to common work-related injuries and occupational diseases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: He also underscored the importance of moving upstream to make workplaces safer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We agree and we have incorporated part of his suggestions into three focus areas that AfA-SHEL will focus on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Second, the support for those who are returning to work after a period of injury or a health episode.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: And third, workplace adaptation and job redesign, to make workplaces safer and more sustainable for our increasingly diverse workforce comprising people with various physical and health needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We also agree with Mr Yong's calls to treat fatigue as a core safety issue and better leverage technology in the WSH space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: These are areas the AfA-SHEL could explore, through prototypes of technological solutions or fatigue management systems customised for specific workplace settings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We welcome the Labour Movement's active participation in the AfA-SHEL.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: On platform workers, Ms Yeo Wan Ling has called on MOM to leverage the Platform Workers Trilateral Group to explore how we can strengthen platform worker safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We have taken the Member's suggestion into consideration, and more will be announced later this month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: They have worked tirelessly to build and to keep our towns and homes running smoothly every day.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Over the years, we have worked closely with employers, dormitory operators and community partners to build a resilient ecosystem supporting migrant workers' well-being, spanning their housing, healthcare and recreation needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In 2024, the Migrant Worker Experience Survey has shown that more than nine in 10 migrant workers shared that they were satisfied with their working and living conditions in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This was the highest that was seen since the survey was first conducted since 2011.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Migrant worker housing has been our key priority.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Migrant workers have built our homes, and it is our responsibility to ensure that they too have a conducive place to rest after a hard day's work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Good rest also ensures that they will continue working well and most importantly, work safely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: That is why we have raised dormitory standards and enhanced pandemic preparedness in recent years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: These improvements include provisions such as ensuite toilets and isolation facilities for better public health resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Improving the housing conditions of our migrant workers does not necessarily mean higher costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Earlier this year, MOM opened its first Government built-and-owned dormitory.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The NESST Tukang Dormitory, as it is called, went beyond regulatory standards to incorporate design features shaped by migrant workers' feedback and improving their liveability and pandemic resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Notwithstanding these innovations, NESST Tukang is able to offer bed prices at below those of dormitories that meet the new dormitory standards and is expected to be financially sustainable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I invite dormitory operators to join the Government in reimagining what is possible for migrant worker housing in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: MOM is committed to working with you to testbed innovations and enhancements for the dormitory industry, as we press on with the construction of our second dormitory that will be in Sengkang West.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Equally important are spaces where our migrant workers can spend their rest days, build friendships and connections.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: To this end, MOM has made significant strides to transform and enrich Recreation Centres, which have seen higher visitor ship over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Melvin Yong have called on the Ministry to continue enhancing migrant workers' access to key amenities and community spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I am pleased to share that building on existing Recreation Centres, we will introduce the Recreation Hub model, and this will expand the scale and range of offerings for our migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This will start with the redevelopment of the Soon Lee Recreation Centre into the first Recreation Hub.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: How we treat our migrant workers in our daily lives says much about who we are as a people and as a society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Together, we will walk alongside every worker as we move forward with confidence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Chairman, I will begin by sharing how we are strengthening our workplace fairness framework so that all workers are treated fairly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: I appreciate Ms Diana Pang's suggestion to make inclusive practices manageable for SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: TAFEP will step up public outreach and education efforts on the Workplace Fairness Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: TAFEP's resources and guides are kept simplified and bite-sized.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Even SMEs with no dedicated HR personnel can easily apply them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Ms Diana Pang also spoke about strengthening protections against workplace harassment and bullying.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: No worker should be subjected to such unacceptable practices in the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Beyond this, we will go upstream to help employers prevent workplace harassment and bullying.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This will enhance the guidance for employers to adopt best practices to prevent and respond to workplace harassment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Too often, women who take on caregiving responsibilities may feel that they are making a zero-sum choice between caring for their loved ones or pursuing their careers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: As Ms Mariam Jaafar pointed out, caregivers who leave the workforce often find it hard to return.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Programmes like Workforce Singapore's Career Conversion Programmes can help them get back into jobs with good prospects.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: But MOM also wants to ease their dilemma upfront by making work and caregiving sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This is where flexible work arrangements come in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: FWAs are much more than just working from home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: They also include flexible load arrangements and flexible working hours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: These arrangements give employers and workers more options to organise work in sustainable and productive ways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Ng Chee Meng and Mr Abdul Malik have highlighted the pressures faced by sandwiched caregivers who care for both children and seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Both Members asked for stronger support for this group, through measures like financial support and leave.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: On financial support, eligible working caregivers can boost their income and CPF savings through the Workfare Income Supplement and the Earn and Save Bonus under the Majulah Package.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Non-working caregivers who have taken extended breaks can also benefit from other measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: For instance, they can boost their CPF savings in their senior years through the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme and the Budget 2026 CPF top-up.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: On leave, many employers have voluntarily introduced caregiving-related leave provisions as part of their strategy to attract and retain talent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This represents about 36% of private companies with at least 25 employees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: However, many working caregivers tell us that FWAs are their preferred means of support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: FWAs offer caregivers the flexibility they need to stay in work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: If a family member needs help with daily routines like medication or meals, caregivers need flexibility across the work week, not just a single block of time off.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: FWAs are thus more sustainable for caregivers to stay in employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: By staying in work, caregivers can secure a reliable foundation for their longer-term financial security.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Abdul Malik has asked for the Government to collect data on caregiver employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We already do, and our data suggests that FWA provision has risen.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: More women and caregivers have been able to stay in or return to work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Based on MOM's surveys, one in two firms offered scheduled FWAs before the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: When the pandemic hit, this changed our working norms and increased the provision of work-from-home and flexi-load FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Now, around seven in 10 firms offer FWAs, even as firms adjust to new post-COVID-19 norms and adjust provision.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: And this has supported our labour force participation rate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Similarly, the female labour force participation rate among those aged 25 to 64 has also risen, from 76.1% to 80.5% over the same period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: FWAs do not only benefit workers, they are a competitive advantage for employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: They widen the talent pool, strengthen retention and support productivity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Dementia Singapore, a leading social service agency, knows this well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: It has fully integrated FWAs such as staggered working hours into their workplace culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: For example, all employees can select their preferred working hours, allowing working parents to start and end work earlier to pick up their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This has led to high levels of staff satisfaction and a low attrition rate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: That is why we launched the Tripartite Guidelines on FWA Requests in 2024.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The guidelines replace uncertainty with clarity, guiding structured conversations on requests for FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: A cancer survivor in her late 50s required a reduced workload arrangement, or flexi-load, to manage her health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: She submitted a formal FWA request in line with the Tripartite Guidelines.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Dementia Singapore then considered it by weighing its operational requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Her work responsibilities were reviewed and redeployed in consultation with other teammates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Her request was approved and she is now on a three-day work week.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: If employers do not consider requests in line with the guidelines, workers can seek assistance from TAFEP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: TAFEP will engage the employer to align its processes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This could include requiring the employer to attend educational workshops on FWA implementation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Ms Eileen Chong proposed making Tripartite Guidelines into law and making provisions of FWAs a presumptive right for working parents with young children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: These moves are a little blunt as businesses differ across industries and roles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: For instance, working from home is not possible for frontline jobs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Rigidly mandating FWAs across the board can stifle business operations and competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: In the long run, this could hurt employment opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Instead, we have focused on more sustainable ways to enable companies to implement FWAs through initiatives such as job redesign support and providing a fair process for employers and workers to discuss mutually workable and beneficial arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Ms Diana Pang spoke about the challenges SMEs face when implementing FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: I wish to assure the Member that support is available.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package provides funding and advisory support to help companies adopt new work models like FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We are also looking to enhance support for flexi-load arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Flexi-load arrangements like part-time work, job sharing and fractional roles may be suitable for caregivers who need work at a reduced load to fulfil their caregiving duties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: However, in 2024, less than half of employees who required the part-time work arrangements were provided with it compared to over 70% of employees who were provided with time-related FWAs like staggered work hour arrangements and location-related FWAs such as scheduled tele-working.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked about grant uptake and outcomes, and strengthening incentives to employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: As Senior Minister of State Koh has mentioned, we are extending the grant to end-2027 to continue supporting employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Given the grant's success, we are reviewing how we can enhance it to keep employers providing flexi-load jobs to more workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This could potentially benefit other segments of workers who rely on flexi-load jobs such as caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Imagine Daniel, a wheelchair user, applying for a job.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: But some employers hesitate, unsure of his capabilities or concerned about additional costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This is where the Enabling Employment Credit, comes in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The Enabling Employment Credit helps employers take that first step by covering up to 20% of Daniel's wages, easing cost concerns.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The results of our efforts have been encouraging.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: To sustain this momentum, we extended the Enabling Employment Credit last year to run until end of 2028.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: At the same time, Daniel needs support of his own.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: While the Enabling Employment Credit may help employers overcome hesitation, the Open Door Programme supports both the employer and Daniel as he navigates the job search and workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Through the programme, Daniel is matched with a suitable role.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: He also receives ongoing support to help him settle into work, such as personalised job coaching at his workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: And if Daniel needs workplace modifications, like a wheelchair ramp to move up to office, the programme also covers up to 90% of that cost.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: It has supported over 2,400 persons with disabilities into employment in the past four years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: More than 80% remain employed for at least six months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This shows that with the right support, persons with disabilities are not just employable, they are valuable, long-term contributors to their employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: But work is both about earning today’s income and long-term financial security.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: While employment helps Daniel through regular contributions to his CPF, additional support can go a long way in easing his financial worries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: That is why, starting this January, we expanded the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme to include eligible Singaporeans with disabilities of all ages.
